english: For a real number $a$, let $f_a:[0,\infty)\to\mathbb{R}$ be defined by $f_a(x)=2x^{2}-3|x-a|$. Let $S$ be the set of all real numbers $a$ for which $f_a$ is one-one. Then the least element of $S$ is ______.
hindi: वास्तविक संख्या $a$ के लिए, माना $f_a:[0,\infty)\to\mathbb{R}$, $f_a(x)=2x^{2}-3|x-a|$ द्वारा परिभाषित है। माना $S$ उन सभी वास्तविक संख्याओं $a$ का समुच्चय है जिनके लिए $f_a$ एकैकी है। तब $S$ का न्यूनतम अवयव ______ है।
solution: $f_a$ is continuous on the interval $[0,\infty)$, so it is one-one iff it is strictly monotonic there
For $x\geq a$: $f_a=2x^{2}-3x+3a$, $f_a'=4x-3$: decreasing on $\left[a,\dfrac34\right]$ if $a<\dfrac34$, increasing for $x\geq\dfrac34$
$a<0$: $f_a=2x^{2}-3x+3a$ on all of $[0,\infty)$, decreasing then increasing, not one-one
$0\leq a<\dfrac34$: increasing on $[0,a]$, decreasing on $\left[a,\dfrac34\right]$, increasing after, not one-one
$a\geq\dfrac34$: increasing on $[0,a]$ and on $[a,\infty)$, continuous at $a$, so strictly increasing and one-one
solution_full: $f_a$ is continuous on the interval $[0,\infty)$. A continuous function on an interval is one-one exactly when it is strictly monotonic, so we find the intervals of monotonicity of $f_a$.
For $x<a$, $|x-a|=a-x$ and $f_a(x)=2x^{2}+3x-3a$, with $f_a'(x)=4x+3$. For $x\geq0$ this is positive, so $f_a$ is increasing on $[0,a]$ whenever $a>0$.
For $x\geq a$, $|x-a|=x-a$ and $f_a(x)=2x^{2}-3x+3a$, with $f_a'(x)=4x-3$. This is negative for $x<\dfrac34$ and positive for $x>\dfrac34$.

Case $a<0$: every $x\geq0$ satisfies $x\geq a$, so $f_a(x)=2x^{2}-3x+3a$ on $[0,\infty)$. It decreases on $\left[0,\dfrac34\right]$ and increases after, so, for example, $f_a(0)=f_a\left(\dfrac32\right)=3a$; $f_a$ is not one-one.

Case $0\leq a<\dfrac34$: $f_a$ increases on $[0,a]$, decreases on $\left[a,\dfrac34\right]$ and increases on $\left[\dfrac34,\infty\right)$. A continuous function that decreases and then increases takes values near $f_a\left(\dfrac34\right)$ twice, so $f_a$ is not one-one.

Case $a\geq\dfrac34$: on $[0,a]$, $f_a'=4x+3>0$; on $[a,\infty)$, $f_a'=4x-3\geq4a-3\geq0$ with equality at most at one point. Since $f_a$ is continuous at $x=a$, it is strictly increasing on $[0,\infty)$ and therefore one-one.
So $S=\left[\dfrac34,\infty\right)$ and its least element is $\dfrac34=0.75$.
originality_note: New: a one-parameter family with a moving kink, where one-one-ness on [0, infinity) is decided by whether the kink lies beyond the turning point of the right-hand piece (way 3, family defined by a condition). Closest known: least a for which x^2 + ax + ... is one-one on an interval (vertex test). Different because: the turning point belongs to only one of the two pieces, and the cases a < 0, 0 <= a < 3/4 and a >= 3/4 must all be examined.
blueprint_concepts: One-one vs many-one: monotonicity, horizontal line and algebraic tests

concept_use.One-one vs many-one: monotonicity, horiz: For a continuous function on an interval, one-one is equivalent to strictly monotonic; for a < 3/4 a repeated value (e.g. f(0) = f(3/2) when a < 0) shows f_a is many-one.
concept_use.Intervals of monotonicity: The two pieces have derivatives 4x + 3 > 0 and 4x - 3, so the right piece decreases on [a, 3/4] when a < 3/4 and f_a is increasing everywhere when a >= 3/4.

stem_review: Read as a student: the family, its domain [0, infinity) and the set S are defined; S = [3/4, infinity) has a least element, so the question has one answer; verified numerically for a = -0.5, 0, 0.5, 0.74, 0.75, 0.76, 1, 2; matches the plan 'decimal between 0 and 1'. Changed: No change.
key_step: One-one on an interval means strictly monotonic; the right piece 2x^2 - 3x + 3a is monotonic on [a, infinity) only when a >= 3/4.
justification: Two ideas linked (one-one via monotonicity on an interval, and monotonicity of a piecewise function with a moving kink), with a three-way case split and no options. Comparable to 2026-P1-Q1 (L3), monotonicity decided by the sign of a derivative on pieces.
